newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS-Junk bonds edge up, trade slow.
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS-Junk bonds edge up, trade slow.

text.p: Junk bond prices closed around 1/4 of a point higher Wednesday, suggesting technical pressure from new issues had temporarily subsided, traders said.
Investment-grade bonds spreads remained unchanged on extremely low trading, as many market players wrapped up business ahead of the holiday, traders said.
In secondary trading, Payless Cashways bonds fell five points as a large buyer unloaded a position, a trader said.
A trader quoted the junk bonds of the building material/ home improvement retailer at 27 from an opening level of 32.
Elsewhere, junk bonds in the paper sector firmed on Wednesday as buyers reemerged after a period of technical weakness, a trader said.
Stone Container paper rose approximately one point, with junk bonds from other paper companies drifting slightly higher.
Elsewhere, Grand Union Co debt fell another 1/2 point on Wednesday, bringing its total decline for the week to three points, high-yield traders said.
Traders said market players were growing more skeptical that a recent $100 million equity infusion into the supermarket chain would be enough to spark a turnaround.

In the investment-grade bond market, prices of the debt of Viacom Inc were extremely volatile. One trader said spreads on Viacom bonds due '05 ended the day six basis points wider, following yesterday's widenening of 10-15 basis points.
Traders said the bonds were buffetted by inter-dealer trading, with little activity seen from retail players.
